finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the `f` query parameter is joined to the root directory without any containment check. filepath.Join cleans `..` segments but does not stop them climbing out of /srv/files, so an attacker can read any file the process can access.
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: name is taken directly from the attacker-controlled query string
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to "/etc/passwd", which is then read
the file contents are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: There is no prefix or containment check on the joined path, no filepath.Base, no allowlist, no authentication, and no symlink resolution. The /avatar handler is not vulnerable because it applies filepath.Base to its input.

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unauthenticated query param `f` straight into os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) with no containment check, so `../../etc/passwd` resolves outside /srv/files and files.go:18 returns the contents; the only filepath.Base guard is in /avatar (files.go:22), not /dl.
